In 2021, WHO and UNICEF entered into a partnership agreement with the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support the expansion of the cold chain capacity, improve information management systems, and risk communication/community engagement with a funding of AU$10.6 million from May 2021 to June 2023. projects.name: Strengthening Maternal and Child Health Services for Internally Displaced Persons in Conflict-Affected Areas
projects.description:
IOM aims to enhance service utilization and improve the Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health (MNCH) outcomes amongst vulnerable, underserved individuals in Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAs), as well as mobile populations.  In alignment with the Universal Health Care (UHC) agenda and national health standards, IOM seeks to contribute to long-term improvements in MNCH service equity and quality by addressing systemic gaps in health facilities, workforce capacity, and community awareness.

The project responds to persistent health inequities in the Bangsamoro region, where decades of conflict, geographic isolation, and socio-economic challenges have resulted in some of the country’s poorest MNCH outcomes. High rates of adolescent pregnancy, malnutrition, and limited access to skilled birth attendance and antenatal care are compounded by a lack of well-equipped health facilities and trained personnel. These challenges are particularly acute in BaSulTa, where mobility trends—such as displacement and irregular migration—further restrict access to essential health services.

projects.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

projects.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

projects.description:

- Address the limited appropriateness of policy, regulatory and standards frameworks by developing a Clean Hydrogen Roadmap and Strategy to lead the long-term development of clean hydrogen in the Philippines, improve market conditions and foster private sector investments.

- Support the development of studies and assessments to improve technical readiness and enable the implementation of clean hydrogen projects that would bring Global Environmental Benefits (GEBs) in the form of total GHG emissions reduction, estimated at 929,665 tCO₂eq, thus contributing to national and international mitigation targets.

- Address knowledge and capacity gaps at institutional and technical levels to identify opportunities and develop green hydrogen projects, through capacity building and knowledge sharing activities and raising awareness in key sectors.
